question: What is withdrawal from caffeine like?

trials.note: with room to reason and write

draft.text: Stopping caffeine after regular use can bring headache, extreme tiredness, nausea, anxiety, irritability, sweating, low mood and trouble concentrating. Australia's Alcohol and Drug Foundation says flu-like symptoms can happen too.
The symptoms can be worse for people who regularly have very large amounts of caffeine, according to Drug Science, a UK charity of scientists.

Australia's Alcohol and Drug Foundation page lists headache, extreme fatigue, nausea, anxiety, irritability, sweating, depressed mood, trouble concentrating and flu-like symptoms, both physical and psychological.
Drug Science, a UK charity of scientists, says people have reported headache, tiredness, drowsiness, insomnia, stomach and joint pains and trouble concentrating.

A 2018 integrative review on caffeine, sleep and daytime functioning says people who went without caffeine overnight did worse on reaction time tasks and were marginally less alert. Its studies also suggest mood worsened.

Drug Science says withdrawal effects can be worse for people who regularly consume very large amounts of caffeine.
Australia's Alcohol and Drug Foundation says reducing or stopping caffeine after regular use can cause these symptoms, including headache, nausea, anxiety, and flu-like symptoms.
Drug Science, a UK charity of scientists, says people have reported headache, tiredness, drowsiness, insomnia, stomach and joint pains, and trouble concentrating.
A 2018 integrative review of caffeine, sleep, and performance says overnight withdrawal was linked to worse reaction-time performance, slightly lower alertness, and worse mood.
